projects.projectName: Vivli AI Form Check Validation & Agentic Chat Automation

Risks.riskTitle: Contractual Timeline Misalignment May Delay Acceptance and Go-Live Governance
Risks.riskDescription: The project is likely to encounter a major delivery governance risk because the operational plan now runs through October 30, 2026 while the contractual end date remains September 11, 2026, with no formal amendment evidenced. As the project approaches PAT, regression, deployment, and hypercare, this misalignment may delay approvals, create payment and responsibility ambiguity, and disrupt timely go-live decisions.

riskChain.rootCause: Testing and downstream delivery activities expanded beyond the original SOW baseline without documented formal contract realignment.

Risks.riskTitle: Unresolved Client Dependencies May Block PAT Readiness and Delay Deployment
Risks.riskDescription: The project is likely to face a near-term delivery blockage if unresolved client-owned dependencies remain open as Sprint 4 closes and Sprint 5 begins. These items directly affect escalation workflow definition, monitoring readiness, test environment availability, and solution fit decisions, which can prevent complete validation and delay PAT entry or downstream deployment readiness.

riskChain.rootCause: Critical delivery components depend on client decisions, environment provisioning, and internal Vivli actions that remain in progress late in the build/test lifecycle.

Risks.riskTitle: Backlog and Front-End Validation Gaps May Cause PAT Failure or Major Rework
Risks.riskDescription: The project is likely to encounter a significant acceptance and quality risk because the current defect and feedback backlog remains large, UI-related issues are material, and front-end validation coverage has been weaker than backend testing. As the project enters PAT and integrated workflow validation, unresolved usability and in-flight functionality issues may trigger significant rework, extend regression, and delay production readiness.

riskChain.rootCause: Accumulated defect backlog, iterative PAT feedback loops, and late strengthening of front-end automation/testing coverage have created quality debt approaching formal acceptance stages.

Risks.riskTitle: Late Scope Additions in Sprint 5 May Compress Validation and Destabilize Release Readiness
Risks.riskDescription: The project is likely to experience release-readiness risk if Sprint 5 continues to absorb both enhancement feedback and late technical changes such as GPT-5 Mini migration, RBAC completion, DevOps IaC sign-off, and escalation workflow integration. These additions may compete with defect resolution and reduce the time available to stabilize the integrated solution before PAT and regression.

riskChain.rootCause: Execution-stage scope evolution and technical change introduction are occurring late in the lifecycle, when the project should be converging toward stabilization rather than adding moving parts.
